couplets.gloss: Just as the letter A comes first among all sounds, God comes first: everything that exists begins with him.

edges.reason: Names the First Lord as the source of the world, as A stands first among all letters.
edges.quote: the world begins with the First Lord

couplets.gloss: What good is all your education if you never bow before the one whose knowledge is complete?

edges.reason: Says all study is wasted unless it ends in worship.
edges.quote: worship the good feet

edges.reason: Calls him the one whose knowledge is pure, which is why a student’s learning should bow to him.
edges.quote: the one whose knowledge is pure

edges.reason: Worship at the feet stands for all devotion, the only real return on learning.
edges.quote: the good feet

couplets.gloss: Whoever takes shelter with God, who is said to tread on a flower, will live long on the earth.

edges.reason: Promises long life on earth to those who reach the feet of the one who walked on the flower.
edges.quote: will live long on the earth

edges.reason: The feet of the one who walked on the flower are the place to reach.
edges.quote: the noble feet

couplets.gloss: Those who hold on to the one who has no likes or dislikes are never touched by life's troubles.

edges.reason: Says those who reach his feet will never suffer.
edges.quote: will have no suffering, ever

edges.reason: Praises him as one who wants nothing and rejects nothing.
edges.quote: the one who wants nothing and rejects nothing

edges.reason: Reaching the feet is what puts people beyond suffering.
edges.quote: reach the feet

couplets.gloss: People who sincerely praise God are released from the painful results of their deeds, good and bad alike.

edges.reason: Devotion to the Lord’s true praise is what keeps both kinds of deeds away.
edges.quote: devoted to the true praise of the Lord

edges.reason: Counts both kinds of deeds as bound up with darkness, and being free of them as the gain.
edges.quote: The two kinds of deeds, which go with darkness

couplets.gloss: Those who keep to the true path of the one who conquered the five senses will live long.

edges.reason: Long life goes to those who stay on the true path of the one who quenched the senses.
edges.quote: stay on the true path

edges.reason: The one they follow is praised for quenching the five senses, the pattern for his followers.
edges.quote: quenched the five senses

couplets.gloss: Only those who take refuge with the one beyond compare can get free of the worry in their minds.

edges.reason: Makes reaching his feet the way to lift sorrow from the mind.
edges.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove

edges.reason: Calls him the one who has no equal, which is why nothing else lifts the sorrow.
edges.quote: the one who has no equal

edges.reason: Names his feet as the one place where sorrow of the mind can be lifted.
edges.quote: reach the feet

couplets.gloss: The rough waters of money and pleasure can only be crossed by holding on to God, whose goodness is as wide as an ocean.

edges.reason: Only by reaching the sage’s feet can anyone swim the other seas.
edges.quote: reach the feet of the sage

edges.reason: Uses seas twice: the sage is a sea of righteousness, and what lies before everyone else are seas to be swum.
edges.quote: the other seas are hard to swim

edges.reason: The feet are what a swimmer in those seas must reach.
edges.quote: the feet of the sage

couplets.gloss: A head that doesn't bow to God is as useless as an eye that can't see or an ear that can't hear.

edges.reason: A head that will not bow is as worthless as a sense organ that perceives nothing.
edges.quote: A head that won’t bow

edges.reason: The feet are where a head proves it is good for anything.
edges.quote: the feet of the one with eight qualities

couplets.gloss: Only those who hold on to God get across the vast sea of repeated births; everyone else stays in it.

edges.reason: Allows no other way across: those who do not reach the Lord’s feet will not swim the sea.
edges.quote: Those who do not reach them will not

edges.reason: Swimming the sea of births is the end of being born, the prize held out here.
edges.quote: swim the great sea of births

edges.reason: Birth after birth is one great sea that has to be swum.
edges.quote: the great sea of births

edges.reason: The Lord's feet are the only hold that brings anyone across.
edges.quote: the Lord’s feet

couplets.gloss: The world stays alive because the rain keeps falling, so rain deserves to be thought of as the nectar of life.

edges.reason: Credits the world’s going on to rain that keeps coming.
edges.quote: the world keeps going

edges.reason: Rain earns the name of the drink that gives immortality.
edges.quote: rain should be known as ambrosia

couplets.gloss: Rain produces all the good food we eat, and as drinking water it is food in its own right.

edges.reason: Gives rain the credit for good food, and counts it a food as well.
edges.quote: Rain makes good food

couplets.gloss: If the rains fail, hunger will grip the whole world, even with the ocean lying all around it.

edges.reason: Pictures hunger gripping the whole wide world once the sky fails.
edges.quote: hunger will settle in the wide world

couplets.gloss: When the sky's supply of water runs out, farmers have no reason to go out and work the land.

edges.reason: Calls rain riches, and shows ploughing stopping when it runs short.
edges.quote: If the riches called rain run short

edges.reason: Farmers are the people named as laying down their work when the rain fails.
edges.quote: farmers will not plough

couplets.gloss: Rain can destroy people, and the same rain can lift those it destroyed back up again.

edges.reason: Credits rain with both powers at once: to ruin people and to restore them.
edges.quote: it is rain again that setteth up those that it hath ruined

couplets.gloss: Not even a blade of grass will come up unless water falls from the sky.

edges.reason: Takes the humblest growth of all to show that nothing comes up without rain.
edges.quote: the head of green grass

couplets.gloss: Even the vast sea would go foul if clouds stopped drawing up its water and giving it back.

edges.reason: Even the sea needs the round of rain, and would lose its nature if the clouds took and gave nothing back.
edges.quote: Even the vast sea would lose its nature

couplets.gloss: If the sky dries up, there will be no offerings to the gods and no festivals here on earth.

edges.reason: Even worship of the gods and festivals come to a stop under a dry sky.
edges.quote: festivals and worship will cease here, even for the gods

couplets.gloss: If the sky holds back the rain, giving to others and spiritual discipline will both vanish from the world.

edges.reason: Ties both giving and ascetic practice to the falling of the showers.
edges.quote: neither giving nor austerity will remain

couplets.gloss: The world can't function without water, which means that even human morality comes down to rainfall.

edges.reason: Reasons from the need for water to the claim that right conduct itself rests on rain.
edges.quote: conduct can’t go on without rain

couplets.gloss: Holy texts rank the greatness of those who give up worldly pleasure and live by discipline higher than anything else.

edges.reason: Speaks of those who renounce while holding to right conduct.
edges.quote: those who renounce while holding to right conduct

edges.reason: The books put the greatness of those who renounce above all else.
edges.quote: stands above all else

couplets.gloss: Trying to measure how great the renouncers are is like trying to count everyone who has ever died.

edges.reason: Those who renounce are named outright and declared beyond all counting.
edges.quote: the greatness of those who renounce

edges.reason: Sets the worth of those who gave up the world past counting, like the number of the dead.
edges.quote: like counting all who have died on earth

couplets.gloss: People who compare what this world and the next can offer, then choose to give this one up, fill the earth with their light.

edges.reason: These are people who made their choice after weighing the two.
edges.quote: those who have weighed the two

edges.reason: The greatness of those who chose this path is what shines out in the world.
edges.quote: shines out in the world

couplets.gloss: A strong will that keeps the five senses in check, the way a hook steers an elephant, is what gets a person into heaven.

edges.reason: Praises the firmness that drives the five senses as a goad drives a beast.
edges.quote: guards the five senses

edges.reason: The goad is an elephant’s hook, so the five senses are driven like elephants and firmness steers them.
edges.quote: the goad called firmness

edges.reason: Such a person is a seed that will come up in the land called the highest.
edges.quote: a seed for the land called the highest

couplets.gloss: Indra, ruler of heaven, is himself the proof of how powerful a person is who has conquered the five senses.

edges.reason: Calls Indra as witness to the strength of one who has quenched the five senses.
edges.quote: the strength of one who quenched the five senses

couplets.gloss: Great people do what seems impossible; small people are the ones who can't.

edges.reason: Draws the line between the great and the small at doing what is hard to do.
edges.quote: Those who do what is hard to do are great

couplets.gloss: Someone who truly understands taste, sight, touch, sound and smell for what they are has the world in his hands.

edges.reason: One who judges touch, taste, sight, sound and smell at their true worth is promised command of the world.
edges.quote: appreciateth at their true value the sensations

couplets.gloss: The sacred writings of the world are themselves the proof of how great are those whose word always comes true.

edges.reason: Those whose speech comes true are, in this chapter, those who renounce.
edges.quote: people whose speech comes true

couplets.gloss: No one can withstand, even for a moment, the anger of those who have climbed the peak of virtue.

edges.reason: Warns that the anger of those on the hill of virtue is hard to withstand, even for a moment.
edges.quote: The anger of those who stand on the hill called virtue

edges.reason: Virtue is a hill that they have climbed and stand on.
edges.quote: the hill called virtue

couplets.gloss: The true Brahmans are the holy people, because they show kindness to every living thing.

edges.reason: Takes the title of sage and gives it to those who have earned it by tenderness.
edges.quote: Those called sages

edges.reason: The saintly of this chapter, who have left the world, are named as the ones who deserve that title.
edges.quote: It is saintly men

edges.reason: Makes tenderness towards all life the reason anyone deserves the name.
edges.quote: tenderness towards every living thing

couplets.gloss: Doing right takes you to heaven and brings prosperity too, so what could profit you more?

edges.reason: Asks what could pay better than the one thing that brings both distinction and wealth.
edges.quote: What gain could be greater for a living being?

couplets.gloss: Nothing does you more good than doing right, and nothing does you more harm than neglecting it.

edges.reason: Ranks it the highest good and its neglect the worst harm.
edges.quote: no ruin greater than forgetting it

couplets.gloss: Keep doing good without a break, as much as you can and in every way open to you.

edges.reason: Asks for righteous deeds without pause, as far as one can and wherever they can be done.
edges.quote: never stopping, do righteous deeds

couplets.gloss: Keep your mind free of stain: that is the whole of being good, and everything else is just noise.

edges.reason: Reduces the whole of righteousness to one thing, a mind without stain.
edges.quote: is all of righteousness

edges.reason: Asks for a mind without stain and writes off all else as noise.
edges.quote: To be without stain in your mind

couplets.gloss: Being good means steering clear of four things: envy, wanting more, anger and cruel words.

edges.reason: Defines righteousness as the shunning of four named faults.
edges.quote: righteousness is a life free of these four

edges.reason: First of the four that righteousness must be free of.
edges.quote: Envy

edges.reason: அவா is the wanting itself, second on the list.
edges.quote: craving

edges.reason: Third of the four, set beside envy and craving.
edges.quote: anger

edges.reason: The list ends with the fault of the tongue, the words that wound.
edges.quote: harsh words

couplets.gloss: Don't say you'll be good later: start now, because goodness is the friend that stays with you when you die.

edges.reason: Calls it the companion that does not die when you die.
edges.quote: the companion that doesn’t die when you die

edges.reason: Speaks straight to the person promising to do better later: begin now.
edges.quote: I’ll see to it some other day

couplets.gloss: Don't ask what good comes from doing right: compare the one carrying the palanquin with the one riding in it.
keywords: why some are rich and some poor
couplets.sensitive: implies a labourer's low station is earned by past wrongs

edges.reason: Answers the doubter by pointing at the rider and the man who carries him.
edges.quote: the one who bears the palanquin and the one who rides in it

edges.reason: Reads the gap between rider and bearer as what past deeds have earned each of them.
edges.quote: the bearer of the palanquin and him that rideth on it

couplets.gloss: If you do good every single day, that good becomes the stone that closes the road to being born again.

edges.reason: Asks for a whole life of good with not one day lost.
edges.quote: let no day fall away

couplets.gloss: The only real happiness comes from doing right; everything else ends up as pain and disgrace.

edges.reason: Allows no joy but the one that comes of it, and puts all the rest outside and without praise.
edges.quote: Only what comes from righteousness is joy

couplets.gloss: What's worth doing is what's right, and what must be avoided is whatever brings blame.

edges.reason: Gives the whole rule of action: do what is righteous and avoid what brings blame.
edges.quote: What you ought to do is righteousness

couplets.gloss: Someone running a home is the support of people in the other stages of life, such as students and ascetics.

edges.reason: Opens the chapter by naming the householder as a support for others.
edges.quote: The one called a householder

edges.reason: Makes the one at home the firm support of the three others.
edges.quote: a steady support on the good path

couplets.gloss: Someone with a home stands by those who have no one: those who have renounced, the destitute, and the dead who need their rites.

edges.reason: Lists those who have the householder to turn to.
edges.quote: The one called a householder is the support

edges.reason: Praises home life for standing by those who renounce, the poor and even the dead.
edges.quote: those who have nothing, and the dead

couplets.gloss: A person with a home has five duties: to the dead, to the gods, to guests, to relatives and to himself.

edges.reason: Sets out what the head of a home owes.
edges.quote: the chief duty

edges.reason: Reduces the life of the home to five named duties.
edges.quote: looking after these five

edges.reason: Third of the five: guests, set between the gods and kin.
edges.quote: guests

edges.reason: Fourth of the five: what is owed to kin.
edges.quote: kin

couplets.gloss: A home that fears blame and shares its food before eating will never run out of heirs.

edges.reason: Promises a lasting line to the one who fears blame.
edges.quote: fears blame

edges.reason: Sharing food is the second condition of a line that never dies out.
edges.quote: shares its food

couplets.gloss: A home filled with love and doing what is right has everything it needs: that is both its character and its reward.

edges.reason: Gives the test of home life: loving-kindness and righteousness are its quality and its fruit.
edges.quote: that is its quality and its fruit

edges.reason: Loving-kindness is one of the two things that make a home complete.
edges.quote: loving-kindness

edges.reason: Beside loving-kindness, righteousness is named as what gives home life its worth.
edges.quote: righteousness

couplets.gloss: If you live your home life rightly, what more would you gain by leaving it for another path?

edges.reason: Speaks to someone who already keeps a home, and asks what more they could gain.
edges.quote: If you live your home life in the way of righteousness

edges.reason: Holds that a rightly kept home leaves nothing to gain from another path.
edges.quote: what would you gain

edges.reason: Tells someone drawn away from home that a home life lived rightly leaves nothing to seek elsewhere.
edges.quote: going off on some outside path

couplets.gloss: Of all who strive for spiritual freedom, the best are those who live a good family life.
keywords: no need to be a monk

edges.reason: The people raised so high here are simply those who keep a good home.
edges.quote: The one who lives home life as it should be lived

edges.reason: Ranks home life first among all who strive.
edges.quote: first among all who strive

edges.reason: For someone weighing striving elsewhere against home life, puts home life first.
edges.quote: is first among all who strive

couplets.gloss: A person with a home who helps others keep their spiritual vows and lives well has more holiness than those doing penance.

edges.reason: Draws the model householder: keeping others on their path and not slipping from righteousness.
edges.quote: A home life that keeps others on their path

edges.reason: Rates such a home life above those who do penance, for endurance.
edges.quote: has more endurance than those who do penance

couplets.gloss: Family life is what doing right really means, and it's best when no one can find fault with it.

edges.reason: Says that what is called righteousness is home life.
edges.quote: What is called righteousness is home life

edges.reason: A good name is the jewel that married life wears.
edges.quote: a good name is its ornament

couplets.gloss: Someone who lives in the world the way a person ought to will be counted among the gods.

edges.reason: The promise is made to the one who lives as a life should be lived.
edges.quote: One who lives in this world as a life should be lived

edges.reason: Raises a life rightly lived to a place among the gods in the sky.
edges.quote: counted among the gods who dwell in the sky

couplets.gloss: A good life partner has all the virtues a home needs and lives within her husband's income.

edges.reason: Gives the marks of a life’s companion: the worth a home needs, and living within his means.
edges.quote: the worth a home needs

edges.reason: Concerns the wife in particular, down to how she handles the household's money.
edges.quote: lives within the means of the man who took her

couplets.gloss: If a wife lacks the virtues of the home, no other blessing in life is worth anything.

edges.reason: Without her worth, a life comes to nothing, however fine.
edges.quote: that life is nothing

edges.reason: Names the wife as the one on whom the whole home turns.
edges.quote: If a wife lacks the worth a home needs

couplets.sensitive: Blames a wife for the failure of all other blessings.

couplets.gloss: With a good wife, what can be lacking? Without one, what do you really have?

edges.reason: Says nothing is lacking where the wife has worth.
edges.quote: What is lacking if the wife has worth?

edges.reason: Hangs both having and lacking on the worth of the wife.
edges.quote: the wife has worth

couplets.sensitive: Ties a household’s fortune to a wife’s worth.

couplets.gloss: Nothing in the world is greater than a woman who holds firm in her faithfulness.

edges.reason: Knows of nothing greater than a woman with the strength of chastity.
edges.quote: the strength called chastity

edges.reason: In a chapter on the wife, the woman praised here is the chaste wife.
edges.quote: What is greater than a woman

couplets.gloss: A wife who worships no god but her husband, first thing on waking, can command even the rain.
couplets.sensitive: tells a wife to worship her husband; could reach someone abused

edges.reason: Praises a wife who puts her husband in the place of the gods.
edges.quote: wakes worshipping her husband

edges.reason: Holds up a wife whose devotion is so great that the rain answers to her.
edges.quote: A woman who worships no god

couplets.gloss: A good wife protects herself, looks after her husband and keeps up the family's good name without tiring.
couplets.sensitive: measures a wife by tending her husband; could reach someone abused

edges.reason: Spells out a true woman: guarding herself and their good name, and caring for him.
edges.quote: A woman is one who guards herself

edges.reason: Speaks only of the woman of the house and what she owes her husband.
edges.quote: cares for the man who took her

couplets.gloss: Locking a woman up protects nothing: her own resolve is the only guard worth having.

edges.reason: Sets a woman's own firmness above any watch kept over her.
edges.quote: by their own restraint

couplets.gloss: Women who hold fast to the husband who took them win great honour where the gods live.

edges.reason: Promises great honour in the world of the gods to a woman as a wife.
edges.quote: they gain great honour

couplets.sensitive: Ties a woman’s honour to her husband.

couplets.gloss: A man whose home has no good name cannot hold his head high in front of those who mock him.

edges.reason: What they lack is a wife who cares for a good name, and so they cannot walk proudly.
edges.quote: a wife who cares for a good name

couplets.gloss: The real blessing of a home is a good wife, and good children are the jewel on top.

edges.reason: மனைமாட்சி is the excellence of the home, and so of the wife, named as a blessing.
edges.quote: the excellence of a home

edges.reason: Makes good children the fine ornament of the home’s excellence.
edges.quote: having good children

couplets.gloss: Of all the good things you can have, we know of none better than children with good sense.

edges.reason: Puts children with understanding above every other gain.
edges.quote: children with understanding

couplets.sensitive: Could hurt someone who is childless.

couplets.gloss: If your children have good characters, no evil will reach you in all your seven births.

edges.reason: Promises protection through seven births to the parent of spotless children.
edges.quote: children of good character, free of blame

couplets.gloss: Your children are your real wealth, since what they earn through their own deeds comes to you.

edges.reason: Calls children wealth, and ties that wealth to their own deeds.
edges.quote: People say their children are their wealth

edges.reason: Calls children a person’s wealth.
edges.quote: their children are their wealth

couplets.gloss: Plain porridge stirred by your own child's little hands tastes sweeter than the food of the gods.

edges.reason: A child’s mess in a bowl of porridge beats ambrosia itself.
edges.quote: your own children have stirred with their small hands

edges.reason: Uses ambrosia as the sweetness that simple porridge outdoes.
edges.quote: Sweeter by far than ambrosia

couplets.gloss: Touching your children is the body's great pleasure, and hearing them talk is the ear's.

edges.reason: Gives children to two senses at once, the body by their touch and the ear by their voice.
edges.quote: Touching your children’s bodies is joy to the body

couplets.gloss: Only people who have never heard their own baby's babble call the flute and the lute sweet.

edges.reason: Says music sounds sweet only to those who have not heard their own little ones.
edges.quote: the babble of their own children

couplets.gloss: The best thing a father can do for his son is to prepare him to take the leading seat among the learned.

edges.reason: Sets the goal of raising a son: to see him at the front of the assembly.
edges.quote: in the front rank of the assembly

edges.reason: Put as a father's duty: this is what he owes his son.
edges.quote: The good a father does his son

edges.reason: Tells a parent plainly what the debt to a child is: to equip him to stand at the front.
edges.quote: to put him in the front rank

couplets.gloss: When children turn out cleverer than their parents, the whole world is delighted, the parents above all.
keywords: my child is smarter than me

edges.reason: Calls children’s greater understanding a joy to every living being.
edges.quote: is sweet to every living being

edges.reason: The parent is the one outshone, and is told to find it sweet.
edges.quote: your children know more than you

edges.reason: Tells a parent being overtaken by a child that this is the joy to wish for.
edges.quote: That your children know more than you

couplets.gloss: A mother is overjoyed when her son is born, but happier still when she hears him praised as a good man.

edges.reason: Ranks hearing a son called worthy above the joy of his birth.
edges.quote: hears her son called a man of worth

edges.reason: Speaks of the mother and her two joys.
edges.quote: A mother who hears her son

couplets.gloss: A son repays his father by making people ask what the father did to deserve such a child.

edges.reason: Holds up the son so good that people wonder what penance earned him.
edges.quote: What penance did his father do to have him?

edges.reason: Turns the father's question round and asks what the son owes in return.
edges.quote: What a son does in return for his father

couplets.gloss: The whole reason the wise work hard and keep a home is to feed guests and help people passing through.

edges.reason: Makes caring for the guest the very reason for keeping a home.
edges.quote: to care for guests and do them good

couplets.gloss: Even if it were the nectar of immortality, you shouldn't eat it alone while a guest is waiting.

edges.reason: Forbids tasting even the best thing there is by oneself.
edges.quote: To eat while your guest stays outside

edges.reason: Picks the medicine against death to show what one should still not eat alone.
edges.quote: the medicine against death

edges.reason: The guest left outside decides what the host may eat.
edges.quote: your guest stays outside

couplets.gloss: Someone who looks after visitors every day will never be brought down by hardship.

edges.reason: Promises freedom from ruin to the one who cares for guests each day.
edges.quote: will not suffer and fall to ruin

edges.reason: Concerns the guests who come each day, who must always be cared for.
edges.quote: the guests who come each day

couplets.gloss: Good fortune is happy to live in the home of someone who greets a deserving guest with a warm smile.

edges.reason: A glad face for guests is what brings fortune in to stay.
edges.quote: cares for good guests with a glad face

edges.reason: The goddess of fortune herself moves in with such a host.
edges.quote: the goddess of fortune lives in the home

couplets.gloss: If you feed your guests first and eat what's left, your land will hardly need planting.

edges.reason: Holds up the host who eats only after his guest has been fed.
edges.quote: feeds guests and eats what is left

edges.reason: Asks whether such a host's field needs seed at all.
edges.quote: sow seed in the field

couplets.gloss: Someone who sees one visitor off and then watches for the next will be a welcome visitor in heaven.

edges.reason: The host who never stops receiving will be received in his turn by those in the sky.
edges.quote: a good guest to those in the sky

edges.reason: Pictures a host always between the guest leaving and the guest still to come.
edges.quote: the guest who is leaving

couplets.gloss: You can't put a fixed value on an act of hospitality: it counts for as much as the person you host is worth.

edges.reason: Refuses to price a hospitable act, and makes the guest's worth its only measure.
edges.quote: It is measured by the worth of the guest

couplets.gloss: Someone who guards his wealth and never hosts anyone will end up saying he worked hard and has no one to lean on.

edges.reason: Shows the cost of never caring for guests: anxious guarding and nothing left to hold.
edges.quote: never took up the sacrifice of caring for guests

edges.reason: Speaks in the voice of one who guarded what they had and ended with nothing to hold.
edges.quote: We have nothing to hold on to

couplets.gloss: Having plenty and still not looking after visitors is the real poverty, and only a fool does it.

edges.reason: Calls neglecting guests a poverty that no amount of plenty can cover.
edges.quote: the folly of neglecting guests

edges.reason: Turns the word for poverty on a man who has goods but no welcome to give.
edges.quote: Poverty amid plenty

edges.reason: Says this kind of poverty is found nowhere but among fools.
edges.quote: It is found among fools

couplets.gloss: The delicate anicham flower wilts when you smell it, but a guest wilts at a single cold look.

edges.reason: A look alone can undo a welcome, so the warmth has to be in the face.
edges.quote: A guest wilts when you look at them with a changed face

edges.reason: The flower that wilts at a sniff is the measure of a guest.
edges.quote: flower wilts when you smell it

edges.reason: Describes the guest and how little it takes to make them wilt.
edges.quote: A guest wilts

couplets.gloss: Truly kind words are those of good people who have seen what matters: warm, loving and without deceit.

edges.reason: Gives its two marks: full of tenderness and free of deceit.
edges.quote: steeped in tenderness and free of deceit

couplets.gloss: A nice word and a friendly face are worth more than a big present.

edges.reason: Rates sweet words and a gracious look above even a generous gift.
edges.quote: to have a glad face and sweet words

couplets.gloss: Goodness lives in a warm look and in gentle words that are truly meant.

edges.reason: Finds righteousness itself in a sweet word from the heart.
edges.quote: sweet words that come from the heart

couplets.gloss: People whose words bring joy to everyone will never know the misery of being in need.

edges.reason: Promises that poverty will not reach those whose sweet words bring everyone joy.
edges.quote: sweet words bring joy to everyone

couplets.gloss: Humility and gentle words are the only real jewellery a person can wear.

edges.reason: Puts humility first of the only two things that truly adorn a person.
edges.quote: Humility

edges.reason: Pairs sweet words with humility as a person’s whole finery.
edges.quote: sweet words

edges.reason: Allows no other jewels to a person but these two virtues.
edges.quote: a person’s ornaments

couplets.gloss: If you look for what's good in what you think and speak gently, wrong shrinks and right grows.

edges.reason: Says sweet words, joined with seeking the good, make wrongs wear away.
edges.quote: wrongs will wear away

couplets.gloss: Gentle words that are also useful do good to the person who says them as well as to the hearer.

edges.reason: Asks for words both useful and gentle, and says such words pay.
edges.quote: Words that are useful and never part from courtesy

couplets.gloss: Gentle words with no pettiness in them bring happiness now and after death.

edges.reason: Promises a return on such words in both this life and the next.
edges.quote: bring joy in the next life and in this one

couplets.gloss: Why would anyone who has felt how good gentle words are keep on using cruel ones?

edges.reason: Asks why anyone who knows the better way would still use hard words.
edges.quote: why use hard words?

edges.reason: Appeals to how good such words feel to anyone who has known them.
edges.quote: what joy sweet words bring

couplets.gloss: Using hurtful words when gentle ones would do is like picking sour fruit when the sweet is right there.

edges.reason: Treats a hard word as a plain bad choice when a sweet one was at hand.
edges.quote: To speak harsh words when sweet ones are there

edges.reason: Sweet words are what the harsh speaker leaves hanging on the tree.
edges.quote: sweet ones are there

edges.reason: Sweet words are ripe fruit and hard words unripe, and one chooses between them.
edges.quote: picking unripe fruit when ripe fruit is there

couplets.gloss: Help given when nothing was owed is more than heaven and earth together could pay back.

edges.reason: Sets an unowed kindness beyond what earth and heaven could repay.
edges.quote: even earth and sky are hardly a fair return

couplets.gloss: Help given at the moment you need it may be small, but it is worth more than the whole world.
keywords: being there at the right time

edges.reason: Measures a good deed by its timing, not by its size.
edges.quote: A good deed done at the right time

edges.reason: Tells the one who was helped in need not to judge the help by how small it looks.
edges.quote: though small, is far greater than the world

couplets.gloss: Help given with no thought of what you'll get back is, when weighed, bigger than the ocean.

edges.reason: Praises help that never looks for anything back.
edges.quote: help given with no thought of return

edges.reason: Needs the sea as the only thing big enough to compare with such help.
edges.quote: greater than the sea

edges.reason: Tells one who gets nothing back that help is greatest when it looks for no return.
edges.quote: no thought of return

couplets.gloss: Even if the help was as small as a grain of millet, people who understand its value treat it as big as a palm tree.

edges.reason: Those who know its worth see a small good as something towering.
edges.quote: those who know its worth

edges.reason: Sets the tiny seed against the tall palm to show the distance between the help and the debt.
edges.quote: the size of a millet seed

edges.reason: Shows the one who received small help how to hold it: as a palm tree, not a seed.
edges.quote: take it as the size of a palmyra

couplets.gloss: The worth of a favour doesn't lie in the favour itself but in the character of the person who received it.

edges.reason: Says the measure is set by the worth of the receiver and not by the size of the help.
edges.quote: the worth of those who received it

couplets.gloss: Never forget the friendship of good people, and never abandon those who stood by you in hard times.

edges.reason: Forbids turning away from those who helped one through trouble.
edges.quote: Don’t give up the friendship of those who stood by you in trouble

edges.reason: Asks that the bond with the stainless never be forgotten.
edges.quote: Don’t forget the bond of the stainless

edges.reason: Gives the plain rule to anyone who was rescued: do not drop the one who helped.
edges.quote: those who stood by you in trouble

couplets.gloss: People remember for all their lives to come the friends who wiped away their pain.

edges.reason: Makes the memory of a rescuer last through every birth.
edges.quote: people remember the friendship

edges.reason: Tells the one who was rescued how long the debt runs.
edges.quote: those who wiped away their sorrow

couplets.gloss: It's wrong to forget a good turn, and right to forget a bad one straight away.
couplets.sensitive: counsels forgetting an injury at once; could reach someone being mistreated

edges.reason: Says forgetting a good deed is not good.
edges.quote: It is not good to forget a good deed

edges.reason: Asks for an ill turn to be forgotten the day it happens.
edges.quote: forget what is not good, that very day

couplets.gloss: Even a deadly hurt fades away the moment you recall one good thing the person did for you.
couplets.sensitive: asks the gravely injured to forgive for one past kindness; could reach someone abused

edges.reason: One remembered kindness outweighs the worst injury the same person has done.
edges.quote: when you recall one good thing they did

couplets.gloss: There's a way out for someone who has done every other wrong, but none for someone who destroys a kindness.

edges.reason: Rates it the one crime with no way back.
edges.quote: There is no escape for the man who killed the good done to him

couplets.gloss: Fairness is the only real good: treating everyone as they deserve, friend or enemy alike.

edges.reason: Says what it is: each side its due.
edges.quote: give each side its due

couplets.gloss: The wealth of a fair person doesn't shrink and stays a protection for their descendants.

edges.reason: Promises the upright gains that last and strengthen those who come after.
edges.quote: a strength to those who come after

couplets.gloss: Even if it brings nothing but gain, drop at once any profit that comes from being unfair.

edges.reason: Refuses gain won by leaving the middle, even where it promises nothing but good.
edges.quote: gain that comes from leaving the middle

edges.reason: Speaks straight to anyone offered a profit for bending the rules: do not touch it.
edges.quote: let go at once

couplets.gloss: Whether someone was fair or not can be seen from what they leave behind them.

edges.reason: Gives a test of the fair and the unfair: what they leave behind shows which they were.
edges.quote: are known by their offspring

couplets.gloss: Ups and downs come to everyone, but wise people are marked by a heart that doesn't bend.

edges.reason: Whatever loss or gain comes, the heart that doesn’t lean is what the worthy are known by.
edges.quote: A heart that doesn’t lean

couplets.gloss: When your heart leaves fairness behind and leans to wrong, know that you are about to be ruined.

edges.reason: Reads the first step from the middle as a sign that ruin is close.
edges.quote: If your heart leaves the middle

couplets.gloss: People don't look down on someone who has become poor through staying fair and honest.

edges.reason: Says the world does not count the fall of one who stayed in the middle as ruin.
edges.quote: The world does not count it ruin

couplets.gloss: A fair-minded person should be like a level weighing scale, tilting to neither side.

edges.reason: Asks the worthy to lean to neither side.
edges.quote: leaning to neither side

edges.reason: The straight beam that weighs justly is what a fair mind should resemble.
edges.quote: the balance that rests level and then weighs true

couplets.gloss: Speaking straight is only real fairness if there's no bend in your heart behind it.

edges.reason: Grants uprightness to the words of one with no bend within.
edges.quote: speech that does not bend

couplets.gloss: A trader prospers when he treats other people's interests as carefully as his own.

edges.reason: Calls it good trade to care for others’ goods as one’s own.
edges.quote: care for others’ goods as their own

couplets.gloss: Self-restraint takes you to the gods; letting yourself go drops you into deep darkness.

edges.reason: Sets the immortals against deep darkness as the two ends of the road.
edges.quote: Restraint will carry you among the immortals

edges.reason: Lack of restraint ends in a dark that is hard to bear.
edges.quote: deep darkness

couplets.gloss: Protect your ability to hold yourself back as you would your money: nothing in life is worth more.

edges.reason: Ranks it above everything else life has to offer.
edges.quote: no greater gain for a life

edges.reason: Asks that it be guarded the way one would guard riches.
edges.quote: Guard restraint as wealth

couplets.gloss: If you practise restraint knowingly and in the right way, it will bring you distinction.

edges.reason: Says that restraint, rightly practised, is noticed and brings honour.
edges.quote: hold yourself in by the right way

couplets.gloss: Someone who stays steady in their duty and keeps themselves in check stands taller than a mountain.

edges.reason: Gives one who stays in their place and keeps restraint a stature past a mountain’s.
edges.quote: holds steady in their place and keeps restraint

edges.reason: A mountain is what he is measured against, and it comes up short.
edges.quote: taller than a mountain

couplets.gloss: Being modest is good in everyone, but in the wealthy it is a kind of wealth in itself.

edges.reason: Finds it good in everyone, and a further wealth in the rich.
edges.quote: Humility is good in everyone

edges.reason: Tells the person riding high that humility is a further wealth.
edges.quote: in the rich it is a further wealth

couplets.gloss: If you can pull in your five senses like a tortoise pulling in its limbs, you're protected through all your lives.

edges.reason: Praises drawing the senses in as a tortoise draws in its limbs.
edges.quote: draw in the five senses

edges.reason: Such restraint is a saving that outlasts this life.
edges.quote: a treasure for all his future births

couplets.gloss: Whatever else you fail to control, control your mouth, or what you say will bring you misery.

edges.reason: Puts the tongue ahead of everything else one might need to hold back.
edges.quote: guard your tongue

couplets.gloss: A single hurtful word can undo all the good you have done.

edges.reason: One evil word is enough to turn all one’s good to bad.
edges.quote: the good you have done turns bad

edges.reason: Tells the speaker what a single painful word has cost him.
edges.quote: If a single evil word does its harm

couplets.gloss: A burn from fire heals with time, but the burn left by a cruel word never does.

edges.reason: Shows why the tongue must be held: its wound never closes.
edges.quote: never heals

edges.reason: Measures the tongue against fire and finds fire the milder of the two.
edges.quote: A wound burned by fire heals within

edges.reason: Tells someone who wounded with words that this hurt will outlast any burn.
edges.quote: A scar burned by the tongue

couplets.gloss: Goodness itself comes looking for the person who has learned, held back their anger and mastered themselves.

edges.reason: Has righteousness find the path and wait for a moment with one who keeps restraint.
edges.quote: holds back anger, learns and keeps restraint

couplets.gloss: Behaving well is what earns you honour, so protect it more carefully than your own life.
couplets.sensitive: ranks conduct above one's own life; could reach someone in shame

edges.reason: Because it earns honour from all, it is to be valued above life.
edges.quote: guard your conduct more closely than your life

couplets.gloss: Look after how you behave with care: however hard you search, you'll find no better support.

edges.reason: Finds no firmer ally anywhere, wherever one looks.
edges.quote: it alone is your companion

couplets.gloss: Behaving well is what good family really means; behaving badly drops you to the lowest rank.
couplets.sensitive: uses low birth as a term of disgrace, plainly so in the Tamil

edges.reason: Takes conduct as noble family, and a lapse in it as low birth.
edges.quote: Good conduct is noble family

couplets.gloss: A priest can relearn scripture he has forgotten, but once his behaviour slips he loses his standing for good.

edges.reason: Sets it above scripture: what is forgotten can be learned again, a fall cannot.
edges.quote: If his conduct falls, his birth is ruined

edges.reason: The Brahmin is named, and his birth is what is at stake.
edges.quote: A Brahmin

couplets.gloss: Just as wealth doesn't come to the jealous, high standing doesn't come to those who behave badly.

edges.reason: Denies any standing to those who lack it.
edges.quote: those without good conduct have no standing

edges.reason: Takes it as settled that the envious do not prosper, and argues from there.
edges.quote: the envious have no gain

couplets.gloss: Strong-minded people don't slip from good behaviour, because they know the harm that slipping does.

edges.reason: Credits the firm-minded with holding to it because they know what a fall brings.
edges.quote: The strong-minded don’t slacken in their conduct

couplets.gloss: Behaving well lifts you up in the world; falling away from it brings disgrace you never sought.

edges.reason: Sets greatness against the blame that comes to those who lapse.
edges.quote: By a lapse they reach blame they didn’t deserve

couplets.gloss: Behaving well is the root of everything good; behaving badly brings endless trouble.

edges.reason: Sets it against bad conduct as the seed of good against the source of suffering.
edges.quote: Bad conduct brings suffering always

edges.reason: Conduct is a seed, with good as its crop.
edges.quote: the seed of good

couplets.gloss: People of good character can't bring themselves to say anything foul, even by accident.

edges.reason: Those of good conduct can’t bring themselves to say evil things.
edges.quote: Those with good conduct

edges.reason: Evil words do not pass their lips even by a slip.
edges.quote: can’t say evil things with their mouths

couplets.gloss: People who can't get along with how the world works are fools, however much they have studied.
keywords: book smart but no common sense

edges.reason: Says that no amount of learning gives understanding to those out of step with the world.
edges.quote: they are still without understanding

edges.reason: The failing is not moving in step with the world, which no book learning makes up for.
edges.quote: move in step with the world

couplets.gloss: Those who have understood right living and wealth never make the foolish mistake of wanting someone else's wife.

edges.reason: Calls the pursuit a folly that anyone who knows righteousness and wealth avoids.
edges.quote: The folly of chasing a woman who is another man’s property

couplets.sensitive: speaks of a wife as her husband’s property

couplets.gloss: Of all who have left the right path, none is a bigger fool than someone who hangs around another man's door.

edges.reason: Ranks the man waiting at another’s door the greatest fool among all wrongdoers.
edges.quote: those who stand at another man’s door

couplets.gloss: Someone who wrongs the home of a friend who trusts him is no better than a dead man.

edges.reason: Makes it a betrayal of trust as well, since the one wronged suspects nothing.
edges.quote: do evil in the home of someone who trusts them

edges.reason: Counts such a man as good as dead, which the Tamil says outright.
edges.quote: no different from the dead

edges.reason: For anyone drawn to the spouse of someone who trusts them: this makes them no better than dead.
edges.quote: are surely no different from the dead

couplets.gloss: However important you are, what's it worth if you go into another man's home without a moment's thought for the shame?

edges.reason: However great a man is, this one act empties it all.
edges.quote: what good is it, if you enter another man’s home

couplets.gloss: A man who goes after another's wife because it seems easy earns a disgrace that never goes away.

edges.reason: She may be within easy reach, but the stain on his name is permanent.
edges.quote: earns blame that will never die

couplets.gloss: Four things never leave someone who goes after another's wife: being hated, guilt, dread and disgrace.

edges.reason: Names four companions that give the adulterer no rest.
edges.quote: these four never leave

edges.reason: Enmity heads the four things that will not leave him.
edges.quote: Enmity

edges.reason: Lays out in advance, for anyone tempted, what will stay with him if he yields.
edges.quote: never leave the one who trespasses on a home

couplets.gloss: A real family man is one who does not desire another man's wife.

edges.reason: Makes not craving another’s wife the test of a good man at home.
edges.quote: doesn’t crave the womanhood of a woman who is another’s

edges.reason: Asks what makes a householder a righteous one, and gives a single answer.
edges.quote: called a householder who lives by righteousness

couplets.gloss: Refusing even to look at another man's wife takes real strength; it is more than virtue, it is the conduct of the noble.

edges.reason: Not so much as looking at her is both righteousness and full conduct.
edges.quote: The great manhood that won’t look at another’s wife

couplets.gloss: Those with a right to the world's blessings are the ones who don't embrace another man's wife.

edges.reason: Reserves every good thing for those who keep from her embrace.
edges.quote: Those who don’t embrace the shoulders of a woman who is another’s

couplets.gloss: Even if you break every other rule and do wrong, it's still good if you don't want someone else's wife.

edges.reason: Holds it the one wrong to avoid even if all the rest are committed.
edges.quote: it is good not to crave the womanhood of one within another’s bounds

edges.reason: For someone near the line: of all the wrongs one might do, this one must stay undone.
edges.quote: Even if you keep no bounds of righteousness and do wrong

ideaLinks.reason: All learning is useless unless it ends in worship.
ideaLinks.quote: What use is learning to those who won’t worship

ideaLinks.reason: Devotion to the Lord’s true praise keeps both kinds of deeds from touching a person.
ideaLinks.quote: do not touch those devoted to the true praise of the Lord

ideaLinks.reason: Reaching the feet of the one with no equal is what lifts sorrow from the mind.
ideaLinks.quote: the sorrow in your mind is hard to remove

ideaLinks.reason: Reaching the Lord’s feet is what lets a person swim the great sea of births.
ideaLinks.quote: Those who reach the Lord’s feet swim the great sea of births

ideaLinks.reason: Farmers stop ploughing when rain runs short.
ideaLinks.quote: If the riches called rain run short, farmers will not plough

ideaLinks.reason: Giving will not last in the world once the sky holds back.
ideaLinks.quote: If the sky does not give, neither giving

ideaLinks.reason: Ascetic practice, like giving, fails with the rain.
ideaLinks.quote: neither giving nor austerity will remain in the wide world

ideaLinks.reason: Since nothing goes on without water, conduct itself finally rests on rain.
ideaLinks.quote: conduct can’t go on without rain

ideaLinks.reason: Righteousness brings wealth along with distinction.
All righteousness is held in a mind without stain, and the rest is noise.
ideaLinks.quote: To be without stain in your mind is all of righteousness

ideaLinks.reason: A life of good with no day wasted closes the road to further births.
ideaLinks.quote: thou wallest up the road to future births

ideaLinks.reason: Home life has its quality only if it has loving-kindness.
Beside loving-kindness, home life needs righteousness for its fruit.
Poverty never comes to those whose sweet words bring everyone joy.
ideaLinks.quote: The poverty that brings sorrow will not come

ideaLinks.reason: Sweet words, with a search for the good behind them, make righteousness grow.
Hard words and sweet ones are set side by side as unripe fruit and ripe.
ideaLinks.quote: To speak harsh words when sweet ones are there

ideaLinks.reason: Recalling one good deed is enough to end even the worst hurt.
ideaLinks.quote: it all dies when you recall one good thing they did

ideaLinks.reason: Enmity is one of the four things that never leave the one who trespasses.
